answer: One concrete mechanism: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because plume only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. In practice basalt is enforced by the ledger itself: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any willow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
